newsitem.title: UK: Fund buying lifts LIFFE cocoa but shy of resistance.
newsitem.headline: Fund buying lifts LIFFE cocoa but shy of resistance.

text.p: Fund short-covering pushed cocoa prices higher on Thursday, but benchmark contracts shied away from technical hurdles that capped gains this week.
"Funds have very big short positions in cocoa they need to cover," said one trader. But bids were matched by a stream of origin and trade sales, preventing March from surging above 900 stg.
The benchmark contract closed 12 stg higher on the day at 899 stg a tonne while May gained 15 to 922 stg. Turnover was a moderate 4,624 lots, including crosses and switches.
Prices derived support from a friendly report by E.D.&F Man, although traders found the deficit forecast of between 170,000 and 230,000 tonnes in line with their predictions.
Man said in its January report that the favourable weather conditions that swelled West African crops to a record last year were now absent.
Cocoa's upturn on Thursday was also helped by sterling's weakness against the dollar and mark, traders said.
Ivorian analysts and buyers forecast this year's harvest above one million tonnes after good January outturn and prospects for the mid-crop.
One source estimated arrivals by January 27 at over 750,000 tonnes compared with around 800,000 tonnes in the same period last year.
But attention was focused on rainfall figures and pod survival rates in coming weeks for a firmer indication of mid-crop tonnage.
